   Two taken to hospital after bus driver briefly loses consciousness, mounts kerb in Airport Road

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise 中文 A Go-Ahead Singapore bus on service 43E skidded and hit a tree on Airport Road after the driver briefly lost consciousness.
 The 57-year-old driver and a 65-year-old passenger were taken conscious to Tan Tock Seng Hospital; no other injuries were reported.
 Police and Go-Ahead are investigating the crash, and repairs are under way after the bus damaged an overground electricity box and blocked a bus lane.
 AI generated
 SINGAPORE – Two people, including a bus driver, were taken to hospital after the driver briefly lost consciousness while driving along Airport Road on the morning of Oct 30 .
 The police , who were alerted to the accident at about 6.55am, said t he bus is believed to have skidded.
 Bus operator Go-Ahead Singapore said in response to media queries that the accident involved its bus service 43E, which collided with a tree.
 A preliminary probe indicated that the driver “lost consciousness while driving, resulting in the collision,” it said, adding that he “regained consciousness shortly afterwards”.
 The 57 -year-old male bus driver and a 65 -year-old male passenger were taken conscious to Tan Tock Seng Hospital for further medical attention .
 There were no other reported injuries at the scene, according to Go-Ahead.
 The operator added that it is in contact with the two taken to hospital and is cooperating with the authorities in their ongoing investigation.
 The bus lane affected by the accident in Airport Road towards MacPherson Road was reopened at about 9.20am, and work s to repair an overground box damaged in the accident are under way.
 An overground box and a bus stop advertisement panel appear to have been severely damaged.
 PHOTOS: SG ROAD VIGILANTE/FACEBOOK
 Photos of the aftermath circulating on social media show a Go-Ahead bus that ha s mounted a kerb near a bus stop. It appears to have hit a tree and an overground box responsible for distributing electricity in the area.
 The images also show heavy damage to the front of the bus, with its front bumper entirely dislodged, expos ing the vehicle’s chassis, and its front windscreen cracked.
 The headsign on the front of the bus , which shows the bus number and route, also appears to have been shattered .
